title: 3D hemispheric surface buckling surrogate: generalized Swift-Hohenberg film-on-curved-substrate planform with regional cortical thickness gradient
honesty_note: Reduced model standing in for the full 3D tetrahedral neo-Hookean FEM on gestational MRI templates requested by the Pass 2 audit (Tallinen et al. 2016). The GSH equation resolves the sulcal planform (labyrinth, Y-junctions, dimples) on the true 2D surface of a 3D ellipsoidal hemisphere; sulcal depth amplitude is imported from the 2D coronal solver (not emergent). Residual carried as a Pass 4 item.

primary_papers.citation: Stoop N, Lagrange R, Terwagne D, Reis PM, Dunkel J (2015). Curvature-induced symmetry breaking determines elastic surface patterns. Nature Materials 14(3):337-342.
primary_papers.used_for: Generalized Swift-Hohenberg equation for a stiff film on a soft curved substrate; curvature (h/R) controls the quadratic coefficient and the hexagonal-dimple -> labyrinth transition with increasing overstress.

primary_papers.citation: Fischl B, Dale AM (2000). Measuring the thickness of the human cerebral cortex from magnetic resonance images. PNAS 97(20):11050-11055.
primary_papers.used_for: Regional human cortical thickness range (~1-4.5 mm, mean ~2.5 mm; frontal/temporal thicker than occipital/calcarine) motivating the anterior-posterior thickness gradient.

primary_papers.citation: Cross MC, Hohenberg PC (1993). Pattern formation outside of equilibrium. Reviews of Modern Physics 65(3):851-1112.
primary_papers.used_for: Swift-Hohenberg Lyapunov functional and linear growth rate sigma(k) = eps - (k_c^2 - k^2)^2 (fastest mode at k = k_c).

primary_papers.citation: Tallinen T, Chung JY, Rousseau F, Girard N, Lefevre J, Mahadevan L (2016). On the growth and form of cortical convolutions. Nature Physics 12(6):588-593.
primary_papers.used_for: Target of the residual remediation (3D volumetric growth FEM on fetal MRI template); 3D gyrification index as pial-area / hull-area ratio.

ellipsoid_hemisphere.note: Approximate human cerebral hemisphere proportions (length : half-width : height ~ 130 : 70 : 95 mm at R_brain = 50 mm); not an MRI template.

generalized_swift_hohenberg.equation: du/dt = eps u - (Delta / k_c(x)^2 + 1)^2 u + g2 u^2 - u^3 (non-dimensionalised by the local k_c so sigma(0) = eps - 1 < 0)
generalized_swift_hohenberg.eps_definition: eps = eps_scale_at_gw38 * (g - g_c) / (g_GW38 - g_c), g_c = 1.18, g_GW38 = 2.15
generalized_swift_hohenberg.g2_definition: g2 = g2_curvature_coeff * (h_mean / R_mean) / (2.60 / 50.0), after Stoop et al. (2015) curvature-induced quadratic term
generalized_swift_hohenberg.time_stepping: semi-implicit Euler, linear operator factorised once (SuperLU)

regional_thickness_gradient.h_field: h(x) = h_mean * (1 + beta * x / a), x/a in [-1, 1] along the anterior-posterior semi-axis
regional_thickness_gradient.predicted_regional_wavelength_ratio: lambda_ant / lambda_post = h_ant / h_post (Richman law applied regionally)

fischl_dale_2000_reference.note: beta = 0.2 at h_mean = 2.6 mm spans 2.08-3.12 mm, inside the observed regional range

y_junction_reference.derivation: Vertex density of a honeycomb network whose centre-to-centre spacing equals lambda: cell area = (sqrt(3)/2) lambda^2, 2 trivalent vertices per cell -> 4 / (sqrt(3) lambda^2) = 2.3094 / lambda^2. A labyrinth is a sub-honeycomb network, so its Y-junction density lies in (0, 2.3094] per lambda^2.

gyrification_index_3d.definition: GI_3D = A_pial / A_hull (Tallinen et al. 2016; Zilles et al. 1988 define the 2D coronal analogue P_pial / P_hull)
gyrification_index_3d.reference_source: Zilles et al. (1988) Anat. Embryol. 179:173-179 (coronal GI 2.56 +/- 0.08); area-based and perimeter-based GI are only approximately comparable
